What happens to Sarah: Sarah feels normal during routine mid-Mars transit.
Key measurements: Temp 36.7 C | HR 68 bpm | RR 14/min | BP 118/76 mmHg | SpO2 98%
C.H.A.R.M. assessment: No active problem. Values are close to Sarah's personal baseline.
Immediate action steps: Continue normal activity and routine C.H.A.R.M. monitoring.

What happens to Sarah: Mild fatigue and possible sore throat.
C.H.A.R.M. assessment: Several values have shifted from personal baseline, but the pattern is not yet diagnostic.
Repeat temperature, HR, RR, BP, SpO2; symptom questionnaire.
Immediate action steps: Stop strenuous activity; rest; hydrate if safe; repeat measurements; document symptom onset.
Equipment: Thermometer, BP cuff, pulse oximeter, wearable.

What happens to Sarah: Fever, cough, fatigue and sore throat.
C.H.A.R.M. assessment: Possible respiratory infection. Fever plus elevated HR/RR and respiratory symptoms justify additional assessment.
Repeat SpO2 and BP; focused respiratory symptom assessment.
Blood / lab tests: CBC with differential if an onboard analyzer is available; respiratory pathogen test if available.
Immediate action steps: Keep Sarah resting; reduce close contact according to onboard infection-control procedure; notify Crew Medical Officer; review trend.
Equipment: Thermometer, BP cuff, pulse oximeter, wearable, onboard blood analyzer if available.
Treatment guidance: Oral fluids if safe; symptom treatment only according to the approved onboard protocol. Do not select an antibiotic from vital signs alone.

What happens to Sarah: Worsening cough, shortness of breath, chest discomfort and marked fatigue.
C.H.A.R.M. assessment: Possible pneumonia / respiratory deterioration. Falling oxygen saturation and rising respiratory effort require urgent crew response.
Repeat SpO2/BP; assess breathing effort and mental status.
Blood / lab tests: Repeat CBC trend if available; pathogen test if available.
Immediate action steps: Crew Medical Officer to Sarah immediately; assess airway, breathing and responsiveness; start continuous HR/BP/RR/SpO2 monitoring; open approved respiratory-infection protocol.
Equipment: Pulse oximeter, BP monitor, thermometer, wearable/ECG-capable monitor, oxygen system.
Treatment guidance: Provide supplemental oxygen if indicated by the mission protocol; prepare the pre-authorized antimicrobial plan if infection probability is high.

What happens to Sarah: Severe weakness, dyspnea and difficulty concentrating.
C.H.A.R.M. assessment: Suspected infection with high-risk systemic deterioration. Possible sepsis, but not "sepsis confirmed."
Repeat BP, SpO2, HR, RR; assess mental status.
Blood / lab tests: CBC trend; blood cultures and lactate only if onboard capability exists; pathogen testing if available.
Immediate action steps: Alert responding crew; perform ABC assessment; continuous monitoring; establish IV access if trained and protocol requires; document all interventions.
Equipment: Pulse oximeter, BP monitor, ECG/vital-sign monitor, oxygen system, IV kit if available, onboard blood analyzer if available.
Treatment guidance: Oxygen per protocol; IV crystalloid for hypotension according to the approved medical protocol; start a pre-authorized antimicrobial regimen when the protocol criteria are met. C.H.A.R.M. does not autonomously choose or dose drugs.

What happens to Sarah: Real-time physician contact is delayed or temporarily unavailable.
Key measurements: Live values continue streaming to C.H.A.R.M.
C.H.A.R.M. assessment: C.H.A.R.M. maintains the onboard approved protocol and continues structured reassessment.
Blood / lab tests: Use already available results; repeat only what the onboard protocol requires.
Immediate action steps: Open Sarah's onboard emergency protocol; continue step-by-step guidance, measurements and treatment despite the communication delay.
Equipment: C.H.A.R.M. tablet/laptop plus the same monitoring equipment.
Treatment guidance: Continue the treatment plan already authorized for the mission.

What happens to Sarah: Breathing improves; Sarah remains weak and febrile.
C.H.A.R.M. assessment: Hemodynamics and oxygenation improve, but active illness still requires treatment and observation.
Immediate action steps: Continue rest and monitoring; document response; do not return Sarah to normal duty yet.
Treatment guidance: Continue prescribed treatment; do not stop or change antimicrobials because of one improved reading.

C.H.A.R.M. assessment: Sustained return toward personal baseline. Continue follow-up before full return to duty.
Blood / lab tests: Laboratory follow-up only if clinically indicated.
Immediate action steps: Complete the treatment plan; confirm sustained improvement; gradual return to duty only after medical clearance.
Treatment guidance: Complete/continue treatment according to the approved protocol.
